official.deadline_note: No single EC/EACEA-wide student deadline is published: each consortium publishes its own deadline on the master's website. The Programme Guide deadline of 12 February (17:00 Brussels time) applies to institutions applying for EMJM project funding under call ERASMUS-EDU-2026-PEX-EMJM-MOB, not to students.
official.application_cycle: A new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters is added to the list each year; in most cases applications are submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year. The EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue is updated annually.
official.status_note: The official student page states: 'In most cases, you should submit your application between October and January for courses starting the following academic year', and EACEA advises contacting each consortium for application procedures and scholarship availability.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Programme Guide: 'Selected projects cannot charge student application fees. Moreover, projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders.' Student page: 'Scholarships cover your participation costs and contribute to travel, visa, a living allowance.'
benefits: 'Full scholarships are available for the best students' and 'Scholarships cover your participation costs and contribute to travel, visa, a living allowance'
'EU scholarship for individuals: EUR 1,400 per month (max. 24 months)'
'The scholarship will be a contribution to the costs incurred by the beneficiary students and shall cover travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs'
No tuition fees, other mandatory participation costs, or application fees may be charged to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders
Top-up contributions for individual needs of students with disabilities, in unit costs from EUR 3,000 to EUR 60,000
Up to 18 additional scholarships funded by NDICI and up to 3 by IPA III for students from targeted regions of the world
eligibility: Hold a bachelor's degree (first degree) or be in the last year of bachelor studies, and graduate before the master's programme starts
A bachelor's equivalent level of learning may be accepted if officially recognised according to national legislation and practices in the degree-awarding country
Students who have previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible to apply for an additional scholarship under the EMJM
The scholarship is awarded for full-time enrolment only, for the entire duration of the Master programme (minimum one academic year where prior learning is recognised)
Open to students from all countries worldwide; for masters selected from 2021 the distinction between Programme and Partner countries no longer exists and all students receive the same scholarships
Consortia should ensure geographical balance: no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during project implementation should be awarded to candidates from the same nationality
requirements: Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme; EACEA does not accept student applications
An EMJM enrols students at Master level who have obtained a first higher education degree or demonstrate a recognised equivalent level of learning

Compulsory physical mobility for all enrolled students: at least two study periods in two countries, each worth at least one academic semester (30 ECTS, or 20 ECTS for 60-ECTS programmes), at least one in an EU Member State or third country associated to the Programme, and both different from the student's country of residence at enrolment
Compulsory mobility periods cannot be replaced by virtual mobility (distance learning)
selection_criteria: 'Student selection must be organised transparently, impartially and equitably'; selection, recruitment and monitoring of individual students fall under the sole responsibility of the EMJM consortium
Scholarships are reserved for the 'best-ranked students' / 'best students' worldwide
Geographical balance across nationalities should be respected when awarding scholarships
coverage: Participation costs (tuition): consortia cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to participation in the course to scholarship holders
Subsistence costs, via the EUR 1,400 per month unit cost for the whole duration of the programme (12, 18 or 24 months)
Travel, visa and installation costs (explicitly named in the Programme Guide scholarship definition)

Full insurance coverage for enrolled students, assistance with accommodation and other student services, funded through the institutional-cost component of the EMJM grant (EUR 750/month x duration x number of enrolled students)
Special-needs top-ups from EUR 3,000 to EUR 60,000 for enrolled students with disabilities who are not covered by the standard contribution
application_method: Search the official EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue for the master's programmes currently supported by the European Union
Visit the chosen programme's own website, which carries the entry requirements and all steps of the application process with and without scholarship
Apply directly to the coordinating institution/consortium by the deadline it publishes; no application fee may be charged to scholarship holders
official.application_route: Apply online directly to the consortium/coordinating institution running the chosen master through its own application portal, using the scholarship application round it advertises; EACEA and the European Commission are not part of the student application chain.
official.study_mode: full-time (the scholarship is awarded for full-time enrolment only, and only in full)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students from all over the world with no nationality restriction; a geographical-balance rule caps any single nationality at 10% of the scholarships awarded during a project's implementation.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - 'EMJM scholarships can be offered to students from all over the world' and the action aims to 'enroll excellent students worldwide'; for masters selected from 2021 there is no Programme/Partner country distinction and all students receive the same scholarships.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction is published: 'There is no limitation in terms of disciplines.' Applicants choose the programme that matches their field; the EACEA catalogue can be filtered by field of study and by country (Poland is among the filterable countries).
official.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits), delivered as 12, 18 or 24 months
official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious international master's programmes, jointly designed and delivered by a consortium of higher education institutions, involving at least three institutions from three different countries. The EU funds both the running of these programmes and competitive full scholarships for the best students worldwide, and the EACEA catalogue lists the masters currently supported, including consortia with Polish universities.
official.region: Europe / transnational consortium (study in at least two countries, at least one of which must be an EU Member State or third country associated to the Programme); Polish universities participate in the EU-supported catalogue
official.program_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM), Lot 1 of the Erasmus Mundus action under Erasmus+ Key Action 2; Master's level (ISCED 7), awarded as a joint degree (recommended) or multiple degrees

verification.notes: Award amount and cadence confirmed on two official European Commission pages: the Erasmus+ Programme Guide (Part B, Key Action 2, Erasmus Mundus action: 'The scholarship is calculated as: 1 400 Euros/month x DS' where DS is the duration of the Master programme) and the EMJM organisations page ('EU scholarship for individuals: EUR 1,400 per month (max. 24 months)'). Coverage, eligibility and application-route wording taken from the same Programme Guide section and the official student page. The Poland-specific URL supplied in the catalogue entry (https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/opportunities/individuals/students/erasmus-mundus-joint-masters/poland) returns HTTP 404, so the live official EC/EACEA pages were used instead; the EACEA catalogue lists Poland among its filterable countries and includes consortia led by Polish universities.

applicant_utility.summary: The EUR 1,400 monthly rate is fixed EU-wide, so the money question is not 'how much' but 'how long': it runs for 12, 18 or 24 months depending on the length of the master you are admitted to, and it is paid only if you enrol full-time. You compete for the scholarship inside one programme's admissions round, not in a pan-European ballot, so your chances track the competition in the specific consortium you pick. Because no central deadline exists, your real task is managing several separate consortium deadlines that all fall inside the October-January window. Choosing a track that includes Poland is a matter of picking a consortium with a Polish partner, not of applying to a Polish institution for the whole degree.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year bachelor students and recent graduates who want a two-country European master's with tuition and living costs covered and who can commit to full-time study in at least two different countries.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist from the EACEA catalogue, then confirm on each consortium website that scholarships are actually offered for your intake - some listed masters have reached the end of their EU funding and no longer award them.
Build one calendar of the individual consortium deadlines and document lists; they vary by weeks and none of them is a European Commission date.
Confirm you are not a former EMJM or EMJMD scholarship holder, since a second EMJM scholarship is not allowed.
Have your bachelor's degree (or proof you will graduate before the course starts) and a certified translation ready, because the EC leaves admission requirements and documents to each consortium.
Plan for full-time enrolment only, and check that the required two mobility periods in two countries are feasible for you visa-wise and financially.
common_rejection_risks: Waiting for a single European deadline that does not exist and missing a consortium's own closing date.

Treating this as a Polish national scholarship: selection and ranking are done by the consortium under its own criteria, and the 10% same-nationality cap limits places for applicants from some countries regardless of merit.
Accepting admission without a scholarship as if it were funded, then facing tuition, travel and subsistence costs that the EUR 1,400/month was meant to cover.
Requesting recognition of prior learning that shortens the scholarship to its one-academic-year minimum, which can turn a 24-month budget into a 12-month one.
Enrolling part-time or planning to replace a mobility period with online study, both of which are incompatible with the scholarship.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The EUR 1,400 per month is a single unit cost meant to cover travel, visa, installation and subsistence together, so in higher-cost cities it may not stretch to rent plus deposits; you still fund anything outside the programme (family travel, personal insurance beyond the consortium's cover, private language preparation) and, if you enrol without a scholarship, tuition and participation costs as well.
document_audit: There is no EU-wide document list, so a dossier assembled for one consortium frequently fails another's specification - check every programme separately.
Final-year applicants need evidence they will graduate before the master's starts, not just a transcript in progress.
Degrees outside Europe must be shown to be officially recognised equivalents in the degree-awarding country, which usually means an extra credential statement rather than a raw diploma.
Your nationality document drives the 10% geographical-balance calculation, so keep passport spelling identical across the application, degree certificates and any credential evaluation.
Consortia may not charge an application fee - if a form asks for payment, it is not the official route.
alerts: The 12 February date published on the European Commission page is the deadline for universities applying to run an EMJM, not for students.
The October-January window is guidance only; some consortia close well before January, so confirm each programme's date on its own site.
A previous Erasmus Mundus scholarship (including the pre-2021 EMJMD) permanently disqualifies you from another EMJM scholarship.
Only about 10% of a project's scholarships should go to any single nationality, so strong candidates from over-represented countries can be crowded out.
The extra NDICI/IPA III scholarships exist only for specified world regions and do not add places for applicants elsewhere.
EACEA warns of scholarship scams: EU scholarships are never granted for a fee, and application fees are prohibited for scholarship holders.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit your dossier directly to the coordinating institution through the consortium's own portal and receive both the admission decision and the scholarship decision from that consortium; EACEA never handles a student application.
